hints.title: Fixed Gap Traversal
hints.text: Removing the nth node from the end requires knowing the node immediately preceding it. How can advancing ahead by n nodes locate this position in a single traversal?

hints.title: Leader and Follower Distance Invariant
hints.text: If the leader advances n steps ahead of the follower, when the leader reaches the end, the follower sits immediately before the target node to delete.

hints.title: Dummy Head Gap Procedure
hints.text: Attach a dummy sentinel node before head. Position leader and follower at dummy. Advance leader by n + 1 steps. Move both pointers in lockstep until leader reaches null. Update follower.next = follower.next.next to bypass the target. Return dummy.next.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: number of nodes in list (1 <= N <= 30)
complexity.notes: Single pass using two pointers maintained at distance n + 1.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: A two-pass approach that counts length and traverses again takes two passes. While O(N), single-pass is the expected interview standard.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Two pointers maintain a fixed gap of n nodes to achieve single-pass O(N) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Using a dummy node to cleanly handle removing the head node (n == length), single traversal pass, and proper pointer unlinking.
